title: backlog(health): drain #2 — retire criterion 3 of the no-exit class; 5 examined, 0 closed, 5 refused
body:
## Backlog drain #2 — `docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json`

**Scope: exactly one file.** No sibling backlog, no `OPEN-ITEMS.json`, no `config/`, no order path, no Tier-3 file. Plus one Tier-1 CI guard (`scripts/ops/check_backlog_criteria.py`).

---

### Denominator at base sha `943a7192`

| | rows |
|---|---|
| total | 1094 |
| `open` | 331 |
| `kept_open` | 187 |
| **unresolved (`open` + `kept_open`)** | **518** |
| resolved / superseded / wont_fix / invalid | 565 / 5 / 4 / 2 |

### Burn-down

| | |
|---|---|
| examined | **5** |
| **CLOSED** | **0** |
| REFUSED | 5 |
| FILED | 0 |

**Reconciled at head:** 1094 rows, `open` 331, `kept_open` 187 — **518 unresolved, unchanged**. No `status` field moved. None lost, none added.

**Closing nothing is the honest outcome here**, and it is stated rather than dressed up: none of the five met the evidence bar. What moved is structural.

---

### Was there a real class, and did I retire it?

**Yes, one — and I retired one quarter of it, deliberately the quarter that compounds.**

`BL-20260825-KEPT-OPEN-ROWS-WITH-NO-EXIT-CONDITION-CAN-NEVER-BE-RETIRED` is the only genuine class in this file. Drain #1 assessed it and named **criterion 3** — a diff-scoped guard refusing a *new* `kept_open` row with no exit condition — as the tractable, compounding half, declining only because it judged CI-adjacent work out of scope. I took it.

**The hole, precisely.** `check_backlog_criteria.py` grandfathers by ID (`if rid in before: continue`), so an **existing** row could be flipped to `kept_open` with nothing said about what would ever retire it and CI said nothing. That is how the class kept *regenerating*, as distinct from its stock.

**It polices the transition, not filing.** Phase C measured — and I reproduced at `943a7192` — that widening from `kept_open` to **all** carried rows (576 across four backlogs) adds **zero**: every `open` row already states an exit condition under some field name. So the guard need only police the move *into* `kept_open`.

**The predicate is the row's own, not a new one.** `EXIT_CONDITION_FIELDS` is that row's 15-field list, which until now existed **only as prose** and was re-derived by hand twice (2026-08-25, 2026-09-01).

> **Positive control:** run over the corpus it reproduces the 2026-09-01 measurement **exactly** — health 24 / ml 10 / performance 5 / research 0 = **39**. A list that merely looked right would not have landed on the same four numbers.

**Shown to fail, and shown to discriminate** — four runs against `origin/main` at `943a7192`:

| | scenario | result |
|---|---|---|
| A | unmodified tree | **PASS** exit 0 (0 transitions) |
| B | `open` → `kept_open`, exit fields stripped | **FAIL** exit 1 |
| C | the **same** transition, exit condition intact | **PASS** exit 0 |
| D | new row filed directly as `kept_open`, no exit | **FAIL** exit 1 |

**C is the one that matters.** Without it the guard could be refusing *transitions as such* rather than the *absence of an exit condition*, and B alone cannot tell those apart.

**It is not a wall.** Run A reports 0 failures while the census over the same tree counts **24** no-exit `kept_open` rows in this file. All 24 are grandfathered — exactly what criterion 3 asked for (*"scope it diff-wise … so the 42-row backlog is grandfathered rather than blocking every unrelated PR"*). A guard that failed on day one would be switched off, which is worse than none.

**Criterion 4 is now mechanical.** `--all` prints the count through the *same* predicate the guard enforces. A metric and its guard as two separate hand-derivations are free to disagree with nobody able to say which is right; they are now one derivation. Census after this PR: **39 → 36** (health 24 → 21).

**Criteria 1 and 2 remain**, so the class row stays `open` and is counted as a refusal. Criterion 1 is per-row judgement (I authored 3 from measurements I actually made); criterion 2 moves 8 ml rows to `ROADMAP.md`, out of scope for a one-file session with siblings live.

No registry change was needed — the guard runs under the `--base origin/{base_ref}` invocation already registered in `scripts/ci/run_guards.py`.

---

### The five refusals

**1. `BL-20260825-KEPT-OPEN-ROWS-WITH-NO-EXIT-CONDITION-CAN-NEVER-BE-RETIRED`** (medium) — criterion 3 built and proven, 4 mechanised, 1 and 2 outstanding. Stays open.

**2. `BL-20260825-BYBIT-OPEN-ORDERS-UNDER-REPORTS-LEGS-FOR-A-SYMBOL-THE-PAGE-DOES-RETURN`** (high) — **my read was vacuous and I caught it.**
Live: `/api/diag/bybit_open_orders`, 2026-09-02T02:19:56Z, `served by https://ict-bot.duckdns.org`, trader `git_sha 943a7192`.
*Satisfied:* the payload does name which read served each symbol — `order_symbols_cross_checked` = `[ADAUSDT, BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT]`, `order_symbols_unchecked` = `[]` on `bybit_1`, so the symbol-scoped re-read ran on ETHUSDT, the recorded instance.
*Why that is not enough:* **zero rows in the whole response carry `settlecoin_blind`** — 12 orders, 6 positions, none flagged. That flag marks a leg the settleCoin page missed and the symbol-scoped read recovered. So the cross-check recovered **nothing** and the union was a no-op; I cannot tell "it works" from "it is inert" on evidence where it had nothing to do.
*And the demonstration is unavailable:* the criterion wants agreement shown "on a symbol where they currently disagree" — ETHUSDT now rests **2** legs against the recorded 7-vs-9, so the divergent book is gone.
*What closes it:* a read carrying `settlecoin_blind: true` on at least one row. That is the positive control.

**3. `BL-20260807-DIAGPROV-STANDING-AUDIT-NEVER-DRAINED`** (medium) — re-measured, **still exactly 52**, twenty-six days on. `python3 scripts/check_diagnostic_provenance.py --all` → 52 findings. Split, which the row never carried: **D/inert-parameter 26 · B/implicit-input-selection 13 · C/unquantified-universal-claim 8 · A/semantic-substitution 5**. That split is what makes it drainable — the highest-severity group is 5 rows. Repo measurement, labelled as such.

**4. `BL-20260806-ISSUE-TRIGGER-FANOUT-77PCT-OF-ALL-RUNS`** (medium) — re-measured and **worse**: `85 of 100` at filing → **`87 of 127`** now. The issue-triggered set *grew by 2* while 27 unrelated workflows landed.
⚠️ **The share fell 85% → 68.5% and reading that as improvement is the trap** — the blast radius of one issue is the **absolute** count, and on that quantity nothing has been fixed.
*Controls:* the four workflows CLAUDE.md documents as issue-driven (`vm-diag-snapshot`, `system-actions`, `trainer-vm-diag`, `prop-report`) are all detected; `guards`, `board-post`, `pr-opener` are all correctly excluded — the latter two are `on: push` and carry `issues: write` under `permissions:`, which the pattern's trailing anchor rejects. Discriminates both ways. *Caveat:* an inline `on: {issues: ...}` would be missed, so **87 is a lower bound**.

**5. `BL-20260730-TRAINER-JOURNAL-COPY-STALE`** (medium) — **refused for want of access, not judgement.** The subject is a file on the trainer VM, which has no HTTP diag API; access is relay-only via a `trainer-vm-diag-request` labelled issue, and this session's `issue_write` is 403 (a write-scope boundary, not the transient MCP drop — retrying does not clear it, and the two relays available open PRs and post board comments). I did **not** infer the file's state.

Three of the five (#3, #4, #5) previously carried **no exit condition at all**. Each now carries one **authored from a measurement made this session or from the row's own detail** — never invented. That is what moves the census 39 → 36.

---

### Caveats — observed vs inferred

- **Observed on the live fleet:** the bybit route's field presence and its `cross_checked`/`unchecked` lists; the absence of `settlecoin_blind` across 12 orders and 6 positions; `git_sha 943a7192` on the serving process.
- **Observed in-sandbox:** the four guard runs A–D; the 52-finding audit and its split; the 87-of-127 workflow count; the census figures.
- **Inferred from code, not observed:** that the bybit union *would* recover a missed leg. That is precisely what remains unproven and why #2 is refused.
- **Not run here:** `pytest` is unavailable in this sandbox (`No module named pytest`), so the repo test suite was not executed locally — CI covers it. The guard's own `--self-test` is registered in `run_guards.py` and passes (35 cases, both directions).
- The live trader reported `restart_pending: true` (`git_sha_on_disk 75ac56fc`). Nothing in this PR depends on the newer disk sha.

---

### FOR THE MANAGER

1. **No `OPEN-ITEMS.json` row is cleared by this work**, and I did not edit that file. Checked against the due list in the session brief: nothing here satisfies a `clears_when`. The guard is CI-side and touches no register row.
2. **`BL-20260806-ISSUE-TRIGGER-FANOUT-77PCT-OF-ALL-RUNS` is getting worse, not better** — 85→87 issue-triggered workflows. Every session that adds an issue-driven relay adds to the per-issue fan-out, and three such relays exist precisely because sessions keep hitting the 403. Worth a decision: a single dispatcher workflow, or accept the fan-out.
3. **The trainer VM is unreachable from a session shaped like this one** (no HTTP API + `issue_write` 403). That is now a *recorded* refusal rather than a rediscovery, but it will block every trainer-subject backlog row for every drain session until someone with issue-write access runs them, or a push-triggered trainer relay exists alongside `pr-opener`/`board-post`.
4. **Criterion 2 of the class needs an owner with `ROADMAP.md` write scope** — 8 ml milestone-PROGRAM rows tracked in the wrong home. It cannot be done by a file-scoped drain session while siblings are live.
5. **`scripts/ops/backlog_drain_candidates.py` shortlisted nothing usable here**, consistent with the drain skill's own 98%-`not_checkable` finding. Selection was class-first by hand.
